---
title: "selectInput() flattens a group with a single choice"
ref: SHY-03
categories: [Shiny]
impact: silencieux
attendu: 'a "Vegetables" group that contains "leek"'
versions: "All versions of {shiny}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2019)"
---

::: {.piege packages="shiny"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shiny))

options_of <- function(input) {
  html <- as.character(input)
  regmatches(html, m = gregexpr("<(optgroup|option)[^>]*>[^<\n]*", text = html))[[1]]
}

options_of(selectInput(
  "choice", label = "Choice",
  choices = list(Fruits = c("apple", "pear"), Vegetables = c("leek"))
))

options_of(selectInput(
  "choice", label = "Choice",
  choices = list(Fruits = c(Apple = "apple"), Vegetables = c(Apple = "apple"))
))
```
:::

## Why

In `choices`, a named element of length 1 whose value carries no name of its own is read as a plain choice, its name serving as the label. So `Vegetables = c("leek")` does not create a group: it creates an option displayed as "Vegetables" whose value is `"leek"`. The group only appears with two elements or more, or when the element is a list or a named vector.

A second pitfall: two options from different groups can carry the same value. `input$choice` is then `"apple"` in both cases, and the server cannot tell which one was picked.

## The fix

Write each group as a list, and give every option a unique value.

::: {.piege packages="shiny"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shiny))

options_of(selectInput(
  "choice", label = "Choice",
  choices = list(
    Fruits = list(Apple = "fruit_apple", Pear = "fruit_pear"),
    Vegetables = list(Leek = "vegetable_leek")
  )
))
```
:::
